meta.blurb: Jane Eyre is ten when her aunt locks her in a dark red room. Years later, as a governess at Thornfield Hall, she hears a strange laugh on the top floor at night. Mr Rochester says it is only a servant.
meta.bible: Jane Eyre: an orphan, honest, plain-spoken and proud; the heroine, who tells her own story. Mrs Reed: Jane's unkind aunt at Gateshead Hall. John Reed: Mrs Reed's cruel son, Jane's cousin. Mr Lloyd: the kind apothecary who suggests school for Jane. Mr Brocklehurst: the cold, harsh owner of Lowood School. Helen Burns: Jane's gentle, patient friend at Lowood, who dies of illness. Miss Temple: the kind headmistress of Lowood. Mr Rochester: the master of Thornfield Hall, moody, restless and honest with Jane; his first name is Edward. Adèle: a little French girl, Rochester's ward, Jane's pupil. Mrs Fairfax: the kind old housekeeper at Thornfield. Grace Poole: the servant who looks after Rochester's secret. Bertha Mason: Rochester's first wife, mad, kept in a locked attic room. Mr Mason: Bertha's brother. Blanche Ingram: a beautiful, proud lady, a guest at Thornfield. St John Rivers: a serious young clergyman who rescues Jane; he wants to be a missionary. Diana Rivers and Mary Rivers: his kind sisters, later found to be Jane's cousins. John Eyre: Jane's uncle, who dies and leaves her 20,000 pounds. Gateshead Hall: Mrs Reed's house. Lowood School: a cold charity school where Jane spends eight years. Thornfield Hall: Rochester's house. Moor House: the Rivers family home. Morton: the village where Jane teaches. Ferndean: Rochester's old house in the woods, where he lives after the fire. England. India. Author: Charlotte Brontë, first published in 1847. Voice and tone: a strong, honest first love story told with feeling; the first part is about a hard childhood; there is a gentle, gothic mystery; deaths are stated plainly, with no gore; the ending is warm. Bessie Lee: the kind nursemaid at Gateshead. Miss Abbot: Mrs Reed's maid. Eliza Reed and Georgiana Reed: Jane's cousins, one cold and plain, one pretty and vain. Miss Miller and Miss Scatcherd: teachers at Lowood. Julia Severn: a Lowood girl with curly hair. Mrs Brocklehurst: Mr Brocklehurst's wife. Pilot: Rochester's big black and white dog. Sophie: Adèle's French nurse. Leah: a Thornfield housemaid. Céline Varens: a French opera dancer, Adèle's mother. Colonel Dent and Mrs Dent, Lady Ingram, Mrs Eshton: guests at Thornfield. Mr Carter: the surgeon. Richard Mason: Bertha's brother, from Jamaica. Mr Briggs: John Eyre's lawyer. Mr Wood: the vicar of the church. Robert Leaven: Bessie's husband, the coachman. Hannah: the Rivers family's old servant. Rosamond Oliver: a beautiful, kind rich girl in Morton. Mr Oliver: her father. Mr Granby: the man Rosamond marries. John and Mary: the old servants at Ferndean. Millcote: the town near Thornfield. Hay: the village near Thornfield. Whitcross: a lonely crossroads on the moors. Marsh End: the Rivers' house, also called Moor House. Madeira: where John Eyre lived. Jamaica: where Rochester married Bertha. Resurgam: the word on Helen's stone. Hindustani: a language of India. Bewick: a book of bird pictures. Rasselas: the book Helen reads. Mesrour: Rochester's horse. Jane's age: ten at Gateshead, eight years at Lowood, eighteen at Thornfield.

The Gypsy by the Library Fire

beats.scene: Jane hides behind a red curtain with a picture book, rain outside
beats.summary: On a cold wet November afternoon, Jane hides in a window seat with a book of birds.

beats.scene: Cousins Eliza, John and Georgiana gather by the fire with their mother
beats.summary: Mrs Reed keeps Jane apart from her cousins until she learns to be more cheerful.

beats.scene: Jane gazes at a picture of a lonely rock in a stormy sea
beats.summary: Jane loses herself in the pictures of cold northern seas and lonely shores.

beats.scene: A big boy stands over Jane, pointing at her
beats.summary: John Reed finds Jane, mocks her, and says she has no money and no right to the books.

beats.scene: A heavy book flies through the air toward Jane
beats.summary: John throws the book, and Jane is cut when she falls against the door.

beats.scene: Jane faces John, her face red with anger
beats.summary: Jane calls him a cruel boy, and John rushes at her in a rage.

beats.scene: Two servants drag a struggling girl up a staircase
beats.summary: Mrs Reed sends the servants, who carry Jane to the red-room.

beats.scene: A huge bed with red curtains in a silent, cold room
beats.summary: Jane is locked in the red-room, where her uncle Mr Reed died nine years ago.

beats.scene: Jane sees her pale face in a tall mirror
beats.summary: Alone in the red-room, Jane thinks of her dead uncle, and a light flickers on the wall.

beats.scene: Jane cries at the locked door as Mrs Reed looks down at her
beats.summary: Jane screams to be let out, but Mrs Reed shuts her in again, and she faints.

beats.scene: Jane wakes in bed, a fire glowing, Bessie sitting beside her
beats.summary: Jane wakes in her own bed, ill and shaking, with Bessie and a doctor beside her.

beats.scene: A gentle doctor sits by Jane's bed and listens
beats.summary: Mr Lloyd, the apothecary, asks what has made her ill and suggests sending her to school.

beats.scene: Bessie sets a plate with a tart on Jane's bed
beats.summary: Bessie brings a tart and sings a sad song, but Jane is too unhappy to eat.

beats.scene: Two servants whisper by candlelight in the nursery
beats.summary: Jane overhears that her parents were poor and died of fever, and that Mr Reed took her in.

beats.scene: Jane sits apart as her cousins open Christmas presents
beats.summary: Jane sits apart at Christmas while her cousins enjoy gifts and parties.

beats.scene: A tall man in black stands stiffly in a drawing room
beats.summary: Mr Brocklehurst, the owner of Lowood School, comes to Gateshead and asks to see Jane.

beats.scene: A stern man points a finger at a small girl
beats.summary: He asks what happens to wicked children, and Jane says she must keep well and not die.

beats.scene: Mrs Reed whispers to Mr Brocklehurst while Jane stands by
beats.summary: Mrs Reed tells him Jane is deceitful, and he promises to warn the teachers at Lowood.

beats.scene: Jane faces her aunt in the empty room, fists clenched
beats.summary: When he leaves, Jane tells Mrs Reed she is not deceitful and that her aunt is the cruel one.

beats.scene: Bessie sits on Jane's bed as dusk falls
beats.summary: Jane feels both proud and ashamed, and Bessie says she is a strange, lonely little thing.

beats.scene: Bessie kisses Jane goodbye by a dark gate before a waiting coach
beats.summary: Before dawn Jane says goodbye to Bessie and leaves Gateshead by coach.

beats.scene: A coach rolls through rain along a dark country road
beats.summary: The long journey ends at night, in the rain, at the gates of Lowood.

beats.scene: Miss Temple, tall and gentle, greets Jane by the firelight
beats.summary: Kind Miss Temple welcomes Jane and gives her tea and a bed.

beats.scene: Girls in brown dresses stand in rows in a cold, dim hall
beats.summary: At dawn Jane finds the school freezing, with ice in the water jugs and prayers before breakfast.

beats.scene: Jane sits beside a thin girl who reads a book
beats.summary: Jane meets Helen Burns, who tells her that Lowood is a charity school.

beats.scene: A stern teacher strikes a girl with a bundle of twigs
beats.summary: Miss Scatcherd punishes Helen for dirty nails, and Helen bears it calmly.

beats.scene: Two girls whisper in a dim corner of the schoolroom
beats.summary: Helen tells Jane that hatred wastes a short life, and that she should forgive.

beats.scene: Girls in cloaks walk through frozen snow toward a distant church
beats.summary: Winters at Lowood are hard, with thin food, cold lessons and a long Sunday walk to church.

beats.scene: Miss Temple serves bread and cheese to hungry girls
beats.summary: When the porridge is burnt, Miss Temple gives the girls bread and cheese from her own store.

beats.scene: Miss Temple, Helen and Jane share seed-cake in a warm room
beats.summary: Miss Temple invites Helen and Jane to tea, and Jane sees how clever Helen is.

beats.scene: Jane writes busily at a long desk beside Helen
beats.summary: Weeks pass, and Jane works hard, rises in her class and hopes Mr Brocklehurst has forgotten her.

beats.scene: A tall man in black enters the schoolroom as Jane hides behind her slate
beats.summary: Mr Brocklehurst visits Lowood, and Jane's slate falls and breaks as she hides.

beats.scene: Mr Brocklehurst scolds Miss Temple beside a table of bread and cheese
beats.summary: He scolds Miss Temple for the bread and cheese and says the girls must learn to bear hunger.

beats.scene: A girl with curly hair stands before a stern man holding scissors
beats.summary: He orders every girl's hair cut because curls are vain, while his wife and daughters sweep in wearing silk.

beats.scene: Jane stands alone on a tall stool before the whole school
beats.summary: He sees Jane, calls her forward and makes her stand on a stool.

beats.scene: A tall man points at Jane while rows of girls stare
beats.summary: He tells the school that Jane is a liar and forbids anyone to speak to her.

beats.scene: Helen walks past the stool and smiles warmly at Jane
beats.summary: Helen passes with a smile, and her kindness gives Jane the strength to stand.

beats.scene: Jane weeps in Helen's arms in an empty corridor
beats.summary: After the punishment ends, Jane breaks down, and Helen comforts her.

beats.scene: Miss Temple listens to Jane at a candlelit table
beats.summary: Miss Temple hears Jane's story and writes to Mr Lloyd to check that it is true.

beats.scene: Miss Temple smiles at Jane before the whole school
beats.summary: Mr Lloyd's reply proves Jane honest, and Miss Temple clears her name in front of everyone.

beats.scene: Green hills and spring flowers above a damp, misty school
beats.summary: Spring brings beauty to Lowood, but the school stands in a damp hollow, and a fever begins.

beats.scene: Jane runs through sunny woods while pale girls lie indoors
beats.summary: Jane stays well and enjoys the woods, but Helen, who has a lung illness, is moved to a separate room.

beats.scene: Jane creeps through a dark house at night with a candle
beats.summary: One June night Jane slips downstairs to find Helen in Miss Temple's room.

beats.scene: Jane lies beside Helen in a narrow bed, whispering
beats.summary: Helen tells Jane she is going home to God, and Jane falls asleep in her arms.

beats.scene: A grey stone with one word stands in a green churchyard
beats.summary: Helen dies in the night and is buried, and years later Jane marks the grave with a stone.

beats.scene: Gentlemen in dark coats inspect a bare kitchen and a damp wall
beats.summary: An inquiry finds the school's faults, and kind new managers build a healthier Lowood.

beats.scene: Jane teaches a bright classroom of girls in grey dresses
beats.summary: Jane stays eight years at Lowood, six as a pupil and two as a teacher.

beats.scene: Miss Temple leaves in a carriage while Jane stands at the door
beats.summary: Miss Temple marries and moves away, and Jane feels her calm leave with her.

beats.scene: Jane writes an advertisement at a small desk by candlelight
beats.summary: Jane advertises for work as a governess and receives an answer from Mrs Fairfax.

beats.scene: Bessie and Jane sit together in a small parlour
beats.summary: Bessie visits with news of the Reeds and of an uncle in Madeira, and Jane leaves for Thornfield.

beats.scene: Jane sits alone in an inn parlour at Millcote with her trunk
beats.summary: Jane reaches Millcote after a long coach journey, but nobody from Thornfield is waiting for her.

beats.scene: A cart rolls through dark lanes with a lantern swinging
beats.summary: At last a man named John collects her in a cart, and they drive slowly through the dark.

beats.scene: A tiny old lady in a white cap knits beside a glowing fire
beats.summary: Mrs Fairfax welcomes Jane to a warm parlour, and Jane thinks she must be the mistress of the house.

beats.scene: Mrs Fairfax pours tea for Jane beside a cat on a chair
beats.summary: Mrs Fairfax explains that she is only the housekeeper and that the master, Mr Rochester, is often away.

beats.scene: Jane at a bedroom window looks out at a grey stone house
beats.summary: Next morning Jane sees Thornfield in daylight: grey, old and handsome, with fields and rooks around it.

beats.scene: A little girl in a frock chatters beside her French nurse
beats.summary: Jane meets her pupil Adèle, who speaks mostly French, and Adèle's nurse Sophie.

beats.scene: Adèle stands on a chair and sings a song from the opera
beats.summary: Adèle tells Jane about her mother, a dancer, and sings a song she learned at the theatre.

beats.scene: Jane and Adèle sit over a picture book at a small table
beats.summary: Jane begins lessons and finds Adèle lively but not clever, and she grows fond of her.

beats.scene: Mrs Fairfax opens a heavy door in a panelled upstairs room
beats.summary: Mrs Fairfax shows Jane the grand rooms of the house, which are tidy because Mr Rochester seldom visits.

beats.scene: Jane on the roof looks over fields as a door stands open behind her
beats.summary: On the roof, Jane hears a low, strange laugh from the third floor, and Mrs Fairfax says it is Grace Poole.

beats.scene: Jane walks the third-floor corridor with a candle at evening
beats.summary: Months pass quietly at Thornfield, but Jane begins to long for a wider life.

beats.scene: Jane leans on the battlements gazing at the far blue hills
beats.summary: On the roof, Jane wishes for adventure, and again she hears Grace Poole's strange laugh.

beats.scene: Jane in a cloak and bonnet walks a frosty lane at sunset
beats.summary: On a January afternoon Mrs Fairfax asks Jane to post a letter in the village of Hay.

beats.scene: Jane sits on a stile in the silent frozen lane
beats.summary: Waiting in the stillness, Jane thinks of the old tales of the Gytrash, a spirit that looks like a horse or dog.

beats.scene: A great black and white dog pads past Jane in the lane
beats.summary: A horse and rider appear, and a large dog runs ahead of them.

beats.scene: A horse slips on ice and a man falls heavily beside the lane
beats.summary: The horse slips on the ice and the rider falls with a crash.

beats.scene: Jane helps a dark-haired man to his feet in the road
beats.summary: Jane offers help, and the stranger, hurt in the ankle, leans on her shoulder.

beats.scene: The man sits on the stile and asks Jane questions as the sun sets
beats.summary: He asks where she lives and whom she works for, and she says Thornfield.

beats.scene: Jane drops a letter into a postbox in a small village
beats.summary: She posts her letter, and the walk home feels like the start of something new.

beats.scene: A surgeon's gig stands at the door of Thornfield in the moonlight
beats.summary: At home Jane finds a surgeon in the hall, and Mrs Fairfax tells her that Mr Rochester has come.

beats.scene: A dark man rests on a couch, foot raised, a dog beside him
beats.summary: Jane brings Adèle to the dining room, where Mr Rochester lies on a couch with his bandaged foot, and he barely looks at them.

beats.scene: A little girl delightedly opens a box of gifts by the fire
beats.summary: Adèle receives her gift, and Mr Rochester at last turns to look at Jane.

beats.scene: Jane sits straight in a chair facing the master by the fire
beats.summary: He asks about her family and about Lowood, and then asks whether she thinks him handsome.

beats.scene: Rochester laughs aloud while Jane stands calmly with folded hands
beats.summary: Jane says plainly that he is not, and Rochester is more amused than angry.

beats.scene: Jane plays a piano in a lamp-lit drawing room
beats.summary: He asks her to play the piano and stops her after two songs.

beats.scene: Rochester studies three watercolours spread on a table
beats.summary: He looks at the pictures Jane has painted and asks where she found such strange ideas.

beats.scene: Jane stands by the door as the clock strikes nine
beats.summary: He decides the paintings are odd and sends the tired governess to bed.

beats.scene: Mrs Fairfax sews by a window and speaks quietly to Jane
beats.summary: Mrs Fairfax says the master is moody and troubled by family business, and Jane decides she does not mind his ways.

beats.scene: Rochester talks by the fire as Pilot lies on the rug
beats.summary: On later evenings he tells Jane the story of Adèle's mother, a dancer named Céline Varens.

beats.scene: Jane watches Adèle asleep with a doll in a small bed
beats.summary: Jane sees that Rochester is kinder than he seems, and she grows fonder of Adèle.

beats.scene: Jane sits across the fire from Rochester in the evening, talking
beats.summary: Through the winter Rochester's moods change, but with Jane he grows more open, and she looks forward to his company.

beats.scene: Jane lies awake in a dark bedroom while a shadow passes under the door
beats.summary: One night Jane wakes to a murmur at her door, then a low, wicked laugh, and footsteps going away.

beats.scene: Smoke curls along a dim corridor around a candle on the floor
beats.summary: She opens her door to find a candle on the floor and smoke drifting from Rochester's room.

beats.scene: Flames climb the bed curtains while a man lies sleeping
beats.summary: Inside, the curtains and the bed are on fire, and Rochester lies in a deep sleep.

beats.scene: Jane pours a jug of water over the burning bed
beats.summary: Jane throws water from the basin and the jug over the bed and wakes him.

beats.scene: Rochester in a coat lifts a candle and climbs a dark staircase
beats.summary: Rochester asks Jane to wait, and he goes up to the third floor while she shivers in the dark.

beats.scene: Rochester returns and holds Jane's hand in the dim passage
beats.summary: He comes back, says it was as he feared, blames Grace Poole and asks her to tell no one.

beats.scene: Rochester stands close to Jane with his hand still holding hers
beats.summary: He thanks her warmly, says he owes her a debt, and bids her go back to bed.

beats.scene: Grace Poole sews a new curtain in the burned room in daylight
beats.summary: Next morning Rochester has gone away, and Jane sees Grace Poole sewing calmly in the damaged room.

beats.scene: Jane watches Grace Poole's blank face over the sewing
beats.summary: Jane wonders why Grace is not punished, and she cannot find an answer.

beats.scene: Jane stands at a window watching an empty drive
beats.summary: Rochester is away for weeks, and Thornfield seems dull to Jane without him.

beats.scene: Mrs Fairfax speaks over her sewing while Jane listens
beats.summary: Mrs Fairfax says he is at a house party, where the beautiful Miss Ingram may become his wife.

beats.scene: Jane draws her own plain face in chalk at a small table
beats.summary: Jane scolds herself and draws her own portrait with the title Governess, Poor and Plain.

beats.scene: Jane paints a lovely lady on a small ivory panel
beats.summary: She paints Blanche Ingram from imagination and sets the two portraits side by side.

beats.scene: Carriages and riders arrive at Thornfield while Jane watches from a gallery
beats.summary: Rochester returns with a party of guests, and Jane watches them arrive from above.

beats.scene: Jane sits by a window in a bright, crowded drawing room
beats.summary: Rochester insists that Jane and Adèle join the guests after dinner, and she takes a quiet corner.

beats.scene: Fine ladies talk and laugh while Jane sits with a book
beats.summary: Jane hears the ladies speak of governesses as a nuisance, and she says nothing.

beats.scene: Blanche sits at a grand piano with Rochester standing beside her
beats.summary: Blanche sings beautifully, with Rochester close by, and Jane leaves the room unnoticed.

beats.scene: Rochester catches Jane's hand in the hall under a hanging lamp
beats.summary: Rochester follows her into the hall and asks why she did not wish him good evening.

beats.scene: Jane stands alone at her window in the dark looking down
beats.summary: Jane admits to herself that she loves her master, and she resolves to hide it.

beats.scene: A tall old woman in a red cloak stands at a grand door
beats.summary: While Rochester is away, a gypsy woman arrives and offers to tell the fortunes of the ladies.

beats.scene: Ladies whisper and laugh outside a library door
beats.summary: The ladies visit the gypsy one by one, and some come out laughing while others look serious.

beats.scene: Jane sits across a fire from a woman in a broad hat
beats.summary: Jane is called in last, and she faces the old woman, who says she is cold and does not believe in fortunes.

beats.scene: The gypsy holds Jane's hand to the firelight and studies it
beats.summary: The gypsy reads Jane's face and says that she is lonely and hides a secret hope.

beats.scene: A cloak and bonnet fall away to show a smiling dark face
beats.summary: Jane notices the voice and the hands, and the gypsy is Rochester in disguise.

beats.scene: A pale stranger in a travelling coat stands in the hall
beats.summary: A stranger from Jamaica, Mr Mason, arrives for Rochester, and Rochester goes grey with surprise.

beats.scene: Guests in nightclothes gather on the dark landing at midnight
beats.summary: At midnight, a terrible cry rings out, and Rochester calms the frightened guests.

beats.scene: Rochester leads Jane up a staircase with a candle
beats.summary: Rochester takes Jane to the third floor, where a bleeding man lies in a strange room.

beats.scene: Jane bathes a wounded arm by candlelight beside a locked door
beats.summary: Jane tends Mr Mason for hours while Rochester fetches the surgeon, and a snarling sound comes from behind the door.

beats.scene: A carriage drives away at dawn with the wounded man
beats.summary: At dawn Mr Carter treats Mason, and Rochester sends him away secretly before the guests wake.

beats.scene: Rochester and Jane walk among rose bushes in the early morning sun
beats.summary: At sunrise Rochester walks with Jane in the garden and asks how she would judge a man who had made a grave mistake.

beats.scene: Jane answers a dark man seriously under the green trees
beats.summary: Jane answers that she would pity such a man, and Rochester says her opinion gives him comfort.

beats.scene: A servant in a dark coat stands at the gate, hat in hand
beats.summary: A servant from Gateshead named Robert Leaven arrives at the gate with sad news of the Reed family.

beats.scene: A bed with a sick woman and a tray of medicine
beats.summary: John Reed is dead, and his mother has had a stroke and keeps calling for Jane.

beats.scene: Jane stands by the window speaking to Rochester in the library
beats.summary: Jane asks Rochester for leave to visit her sick aunt, and he agrees, a little reluctantly.

beats.scene: Jane folds a dress into a small trunk while Adèle watches
beats.summary: Jane packs and says goodbye to Adèle, and Rochester tells her he expects her to come back.

beats.scene: A coach rolls along a wide road through green fields
beats.summary: Jane travels all day by coach and arrives in the evening at Gateshead.

beats.scene: Bessie in a bonnet hugs Jane at the lodge gate
beats.summary: Bessie meets her at the lodge, and they talk happily as they walk to the house.

beats.scene: Two young women in black sit sewing in a cold drawing room
beats.summary: Jane finds her cousins Eliza and Georgiana in mourning, and they greet her coldly.

beats.scene: Jane stands beside a high bed where an old woman lies staring
beats.summary: Mrs Reed is propped in bed, thin and hard, and she asks whether Jane is truly her niece.

beats.scene: Jane sits by a sick bed while two cousins talk in the next room
beats.summary: Jane stays at Gateshead, where Georgiana complains all day and Eliza keeps strictly to her own routine.

beats.scene: Mrs Reed beckons Jane closer with a thin hand
beats.summary: At last Mrs Reed says she has done Jane a wrong and wants to speak before she dies.

beats.scene: An old letter with a foreign stamp lies in a drawer
beats.summary: Mrs Reed confesses that three years ago John Eyre wrote from Madeira asking for Jane, and she lied to him.

beats.scene: Mrs Reed hands Jane a folded paper with trembling fingers
beats.summary: Mrs Reed admits she hated Jane because her husband loved her, and she gives Jane the letter.

beats.scene: Jane kneels beside the bed and takes the old woman's hand
beats.summary: Jane forgives her and asks for forgiveness in return, but Mrs Reed turns her face away.

beats.scene: A candle burns beside a shrouded form in a dark room
beats.summary: Mrs Reed dies that night, and Jane sits beside her, feeling only sadness.

beats.scene: Black carriages wind slowly down a village road
beats.summary: After the funeral, the cousins make their plans, and Eliza calmly tells Jane she will enter a convent.

beats.scene: Georgiana lies on a sofa while Eliza locks her desk
beats.summary: Georgiana will go to London and marry well, and the two sisters part with hardly a kiss.

beats.scene: Jane sits in a coach window as the green country rolls by
beats.summary: Jane leaves Gateshead for Thornfield, wondering whether Rochester is married by now.

beats.scene: A man sits on a stile in a hayfield with a sketchbook
beats.summary: On a midsummer evening Jane walks across the hayfields and finds Rochester sitting on a stile.

beats.scene: Rochester rises from a stile and holds out both hands to Jane
beats.summary: Rochester greets Jane warmly and says he has been waiting for her to come home.

beats.scene: Jane sits happily in the Thornfield parlour among her friends
beats.summary: Thornfield feels like home to Jane, and Mrs Fairfax and Adèle are very glad to see her.

beats.scene: Rochester and Jane stroll in the orchard at dusk among apple trees
beats.summary: One evening Rochester says he is to be married soon and that Jane must find a new place.

beats.scene: Rochester speaks of a distant house in Ireland and a great sea
beats.summary: He suggests a post in Ireland, with a lady named Mrs O'Gall, far across the sea.

beats.scene: Jane stands under a chestnut tree with tears running down her cheeks
beats.summary: Jane weeps at the thought of leaving Thornfield and the master she loves.

beats.scene: Jane speaks passionately to Rochester under a dark tree
beats.summary: She says that she is not a machine and that in spirit she is his equal.

beats.scene: Rochester takes both of Jane's hands in the twilight
beats.summary: Rochester says that he loves her and asks her to be his wife.

beats.scene: Jane looks up doubtfully at Rochester's earnest face
beats.summary: Jane thinks he is cruel to joke, but he says Miss Ingram is nothing to him.

beats.scene: Rochester and Jane embrace beneath a tree as the wind rises
beats.summary: Jane sees that he is serious, and she says yes.

beats.scene: Lightning splits a great tree behind them while rain pours down
beats.summary: A storm breaks, and lightning splits the great chestnut tree in two.

beats.scene: Rochester holds up a rich silk dress in a shop in Millcote
beats.summary: Rochester buys silks and jewels for Jane, and she does not enjoy being given so much.

beats.scene: Jane writes a letter at her desk with a pen and a lamp
beats.summary: Jane writes to her uncle John Eyre in Madeira, hoping to bring a little money of her own to the marriage.

beats.scene: Mrs Fairfax speaks gently to Jane beside a window
beats.summary: Mrs Fairfax warns Jane to be careful, because a master and a governess are not equals.

beats.scene: Rochester laughs as Jane tells him she will remain simple
beats.summary: Jane teases Rochester when he is too proud and refuses to become a fine lady.

beats.scene: A white dress and a long veil hang beside a window in a storm
beats.summary: The night before the wedding Rochester is away, and a wind howls around the house.

beats.scene: A tall, dark woman stands in the candlelight holding a veil
beats.summary: At midnight a strange woman enters Jane's room and tries on the veil.

beats.scene: The woman tears a white veil in two in front of a mirror
beats.summary: She tears the veil in two, then bends over Jane's bed, and Jane faints.

beats.scene: Rochester sits on Jane's bed in the morning light, holding her hand
beats.summary: Rochester says that it was part dream, but he promises to explain everything one year from the wedding.

beats.scene: Jane and Rochester walk quickly into a small stone church
beats.summary: On the wedding morning Jane wears a plain white dress, and the two walk quickly to the church.

beats.scene: A man in a dark coat rises from a pew at the back
beats.summary: The vicar asks if anyone knows any reason why they should not marry, and a stranger answers.

beats.scene: A lawyer reads a paper aloud in a hushed church
beats.summary: The lawyer, Mr Briggs, declares that Mr Rochester already has a wife living, Bertha Mason of Jamaica.

beats.scene: Rochester stands stiff with his hand held up in the church
beats.summary: Rochester says the wedding must stop, and he asks everyone to follow him to Thornfield.

beats.scene: Mr Mason stands beside the lawyer and nods gravely
beats.summary: Mr Mason, the stranger from Jamaica, says that his sister is alive and living at Thornfield Hall.

beats.scene: A tapestry is lifted to show a secret door upstairs
beats.summary: Rochester leads them to the third floor and opens a small, hidden door behind a tapestry.

beats.scene: A wild figure moves on all fours in a dim room
beats.summary: In the room, a strange figure crouches in the shadow, and Grace Poole sits nearby.

beats.scene: Rochester struggles to hold a tall, wild woman in his arms
beats.summary: The figure leaps at Rochester, and he holds her with all his strength until she is tied.

beats.scene: Jane stands alone in her room as the door closes
beats.summary: Rochester says, This is my wife, and Jane returns alone to her room, sick at heart.

beats.scene: Rochester sits on the floor outside Jane's door
beats.summary: Rochester comes to her door and tells her the story of his marriage to Bertha in Jamaica.

beats.scene: Rochester speaks urgently with Jane's hands in his
beats.summary: He asks Jane to live with him abroad as his wife, though it is against the law.

beats.scene: Jane stands upright, tears on her face, in a dim room
beats.summary: Jane refuses, and decides in the night that she must leave Thornfield.

beats.scene: Jane in a dark dress ties a small bundle by candlelight at dawn
